question: to the Commission Jadwiga Wiśniewska (ECR) Subject:

The global overproduction of steel and ever-increasing steel imports to Europe limit the competitiveness of the EU’s steel industry, which is unable to compete with cheap imported steel from countries that do not have to comply with the excessive climate standards arising mainly from the EU ETS. Under a regulation protecting the EU’s steel industry from the negative effects of global overcapacity of steel (2025/0726(COD)), the Commission should urgently adopt an implementing regulation that defines quotas for importing steel for third countries. The new EU trade policy tool will only be effective if it is watertight and based on mechanisms that tangibly reduce the influx of steel from outside the EU. 1.

Is the Commission planning to impose tariff rate quotas (TRQs) on third countries in order to tangibly reduce imports from countries that are flooding the EU with cheap imported steel and, if so, how does it plan to do so?

Ukraine exports significant quantities of steel to the EU. Therefore, quotas for steel imports from Ukraine should be based on an objective share of imports to the EU in 2022–2024. Does the Commission plan to apply specific exceptions or derogations to imports of Ukrainian steel?

Does the Commission intend to ensure the credibility and effectiveness of the future instrument by not using the ‘exceptional circumstances’ clause for EU candidate countries as a basis for increasing their allocations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.7.2026) The Regulation (EU) 2026/1384 addressing the negative trade-related effects of global overcapacity on the EU steel market introduces tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) applicable from 1 July 20261. It provides for 18.3 million tonnes of duty-free imports, while imports exceeding the applicable quotas are subject to a 50% duty. It also introduces a ‘melt and pour’ rule to strengthen transparency. On 30 June 2026, the Commission adopted an Implementing Act2, which entered into force on 1 July 2026, establishing the allocation of the TRQs among third countries in accordance with the criteria and procedures laid down in the Regulation, following an objective and fair methodology with a view to ensuring that the instrument effectively addresses the impact of global steel overcapacity while remaining consistent with the EU's international obligations. With regard to Ukraine, the Commission’s Implementing Act applies the provisions of Article 5(1)(i) of Regulation (EU) 2026/2384 and ensures that the quotas take into account the situation of a candidate country facing an exceptional and immediate security situation. The Commission remains committed to ensuring that the new instrument is implemented in an effective, transparent and proportionate manner and provides meaningful protection for the EU steel market.
